title: Oil Rises as US-Iran Conflict Escalates, Hormuz Toll Plan Scrapped
content: US strikes on Iran entered a seventh consecutive night by 17 July 2026, widening a conflict that began in early July, as Iran hit tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and fired on Qatar, Kuwait and Jordan. Brent crude rose to about $84.73/bbl on 14 July and WTI to $79.34, up roughly 1.5-1.7% on the session, after President Trump threatened a 20% toll on Hormuz cargo before dropping the plan amid shipping-industry opposition; the IMO called mandatory tolls illegal. With around a fifth of global oil flows transiting the strait, the standoff kept a geopolitical risk premium across crude, FX and rates, and reinforced BoE warnings that the energy shock complicates the inflation outlook.

title: Global Chip Stocks Slump as China's Kimi K3 Model Stokes AI-Spend Doubts
content: Chinese startup Moonshot AI unveiled Kimi K3, a 2.8trn-parameter open-weight model rivalling top US systems, on 17 July 2026, triggering a global chip-stock rout reminiscent of 2025's DeepSeek shock. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell over 20% from its June peak, Taiwan's market dropped 6% and Japan's 4%; Nvidia slid as much as 5% intraday before paring losses, while TSMC fell 7% despite reporting a 77% jump in quarterly operating profit. The Nasdaq Composite ended the week down 2.9% and the S&P 500 off 1.6%. The selloff reflected concern that cheaper frontier AI models could undercut demand assumptions underpinning years of heavy capex in AI infrastructure and high-end chips.

title: US June CPI Cools Sharply to 3.5%, Fed Rate-Hike Bets Pared Back
content: US CPI data released 14 July 2026 showed headline inflation fell 0.4% m/m, the steepest monthly drop since April 2020, taking the annual rate to 3.5% versus a 3.8% forecast and May's 4.2%. Core CPI was flat m/m at 2.6% y/y, also below consensus. A 5.7% monthly slide in energy prices, linked to the earlier Middle East ceasefire window, drove the surprise. UST yields fell, with the 10-year easing to around 4.58% and the 2-year to about 4.19%, as traders trimmed bets on a hike at the 31 July FOMC meeting, though a September move stayed priced near 60%. The USD eased on the repricing.
